title: Agent Orchestration, Reliability & Human-in-the-Loop
description: Architect stateful agent workflows, checkpointing, tool permissions, human approval gates, and bounded execution in .NET.

data.text: The Architecture of Reliable Agent Systems

A common mistake in early AI development is deploying an unconstrained while-loop that prompts an LLM until it decides to stop. In production enterprise applications, this leads to non-deterministic behavior, infinite loops, runaway API costs, and dangerous actions executed without verification. Enterprise agents need predictable execution, state recovery, and controlled autonomy.

data.title: .NET Architectural Principle
data.text: Start with an explicit workflow or state machine as the architectural baseline. Introduce LLM-driven autonomous decisions only at specific decision states where flexible judgment provides genuine business value. Keep state transitions, authorization, persistence, and external side-effects strictly governed by deterministic .NET code.

Bounded retries, loop limiters, and human escalation

data.text: Microsoft Agent Framework & Semantic Kernel Evolution

The Microsoft Agent Framework builds upon Semantic Kernel to provide standardized agent abstractions (ChatCompletionAgent, OpenAIAssistantAgent), workflow graphs, and multi-agent group chats. When using experimental agent APIs, maintain an abstraction barrier so that underlying SDK changes don't disrupt your core business logic.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Enterprise agents must be built on deterministic state machines with bounded loops
Always enforce maximum tool-call step counts and timeouts to prevent runaway loops
Persist execution state in durable checkpoints to survive application restarts
Enforce Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval gates before executing high-consequence tools
Choose the appropriate topology: Sequential pipelines, Concurrent evaluation, or Supervisor handoffs
data.takeaway: Predictable autonomy is the hallmark of enterprise AI engineering. By combining state machines, checkpointing, and human approval gates, you gain the benefits of LLM reasoning without sacrificing system reliability.
